title: A product-preserving derived functor commutes with derived limits

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be additive, commute with countable products, and admit a right derived functor $RF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For every countable inverse system $(K_n)$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, the derived category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with derived limit $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit], $RF(K)$ is a derived limit of $(RF(K_n))$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$: applying $RF$ to a Roos triangle of $K$ (products taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$) gives a Roos triangle of $(RF(K_n))$ (products taken in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$); that is, $RF(K)=R\varprojlim_nRF(K_n)$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit] (an object with such a triangle, not a canonical comparison map).

proof.text: Choose a Roos triangle for the derived limit $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ as in [def-weil-derived-limit]. Its first two non-shifted terms are the product $\prod_nK_n$ and the same product, and its middle map is $1-s$ formed from the transition maps.

source.place: Tag 08U1, label lemma-RF-commutes-with-Rlim, statement and proof

proof.text: Represent every $K_n$ by a K-injective complex $I_n^\bullet$. The termwise product $\prod_n I_n^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))$ by [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]. Applying the K-injective construction of the right derived functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] gives $RF(\prod_nK_n)=F(\prod_n I_n^\bullet)$. The hypothesis that $F$ commutes with countable products identifies this complex with $\prod_nF(I_n^\bullet)$, and the termwise-product clause of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] identifies the latter with $\prod_nRF(K_n)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$.

source.place: Tag 08U1, label lemma-RF-commutes-with-Rlim, proof paragraphs on K-injective representatives and products

proof.text: By [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], $RF$ has the shift commutation and triangulated-functor structure required by [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map]. Step 2 identifies the image of each product vertex with the product of the $RF(K_n)$, so that theorem sends the Roos triangle of Step 1 to a homotopy-limit cone for $(RF(K_n))$. Thus $RF(K)$, with the image of the Roos triangle, is a derived limit of $(RF(K_n))$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit], i.e. $RF(K)=R\varprojlim_nRF(K_n)$. (The products in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ required by [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map] exist by Step 2, every object being represented by a K-injective complex.)

lean.statement: theorem rightDerivedFunctor_isDerivedLimitTriangle (X : Scheme.{u}) (F : X.Modules ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) [F.Additive] [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) F] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions X.Modules] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasDerivedCategory X.Modules] [HasDerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}] {K : ℕ → DerivedCategory X.Modules} (f : ∀ n, K (n + 1) ⟶ K n) (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ K) (δ : ∏ᶜ K ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (h : CategoryTheory.IsDerivedLimitTriangle f L p δ) : ∃ e : F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj (∏ᶜ K) ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n => F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj (K n)), (∀ n, e.hom ≫ Pi.π _ n = F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (Pi.π K n)) ∧ CategoryTheory.IsDerivedLimitTriangle (fun n => F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (f n)) (F.rightDerivedFunctor.obj L) (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map p ≫ e.hom) (e.inv ≫ F.rightDerivedFunctor.map δ ≫ (F.rightDerivedFunctor.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app L)
